question: Your team uses Claude Code to write an onboarding guide for a payments service. Claude Code sends one subagent to read the source code, one to read the test suite, and one to query the team's design-decision wiki through an MCP server. The wiki subagent's calls keep timing out after local retries, so it returns the error with its attempted queries, while the other two subagents return full findings. How should Claude Code structure the synthesized onboarding guide?

options.text: Open the guide with one generic line saying that the wiki search was unavailable, and then present every section that follows as equally complete and well-supported.
options.reason: A generic status hides useful context, and marking every section as well-supported hides which topic areas actually have gaps, so readers cannot tell supported findings from missing ones.

options.text: Write the design rationale sections from patterns that Claude Code infers in the source code and tests, and present them as documented team decisions.
options.reason: This hides the gap that the unavailable wiki caused and presents guesses as supported findings, which is the opposite of annotating coverage gaps.

options.text: Annotate each section as well-supported by the code and tests or as a coverage gap, naming the design rationale as missing because the wiki was unavailable.
options.reason: The guide says synthesis output should carry coverage annotations that show which findings are well-supported and which topic areas have gaps due to unavailable sources.

options.text: State in the guide that the team has recorded no design decisions for the payments service, because the wiki subagent returned no design findings.
options.reason: This treats an access failure (a timeout) as a valid empty result, which the guide says must be kept distinct so that the right decision can be made.
